Pseudo-bulking with optimal number of Pseudotime based bins

Source: R/sc.squeeze.R
sc.squeeze.Rd

sc.squeeze() discretizes a continuous time series column into bins of equal width. It automatically calculates the optimal number of bins using one of the supported methods.

The bins of a path divide the range of its pseudotime into intervals of equal width (split_bins divides large ones further), and each cell goes to the bin whose interval holds its pseudotime. As in Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.1, "bins are structured as left-closed and right-open intervals, except for the last bin, which is closed on both ends": a cell whose pseudotime is the bound of two bins goes to the later one. The bounds of the intervals are stored in the scmp_l_bound and scmp_u_bound columns of the bin metadata (see cDense()).

The paths are binned, and their bins stored, in the order of the levels of the path column when it is a factor, and otherwise in the C-locale order of the path labels (byte order: digits before uppercase letters, uppercase before lowercase), whatever the collation of the R session. sc.set.poly() takes the first path as the reference unless its reference argument names another one.

sc.squeeze(
  scmpObj,
  ptime_col = scmpObj@Parameters@ptime_col,
  path_col = scmpObj@Parameters@path_col,
  bin_method = "Sturges",
  drop_fac = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  bin_mem_col = "scmp_bin_members",
  bin_col = "scmp_bin",
  bin_size_col = "scmp_bin_size",
  bin_ptime_col = "scmp_binned_pseudotime",
  split_bins = FALSE,
  prune_bins = FALSE,
  assay_name = "counts",
  drop_trails = FALSE,
  aggregate = "sum",
  fill_gaps = FALSE,
  additional_params = list(use_unique_time_points = FALSE)
)

Arguments

scmpObj

An object of class ScMaSigPro.

ptime_col

A character string representing the column name for inferred Pseudotime values in 'Sparse' data. (Default is "Pseudotime").

path_col

A character string representing the column name for branching path assignment in 'Sparse' or 'Dense' data. (Default is path_prefix).

bin_method

A character string representing the algorithm used for binning. Available options: "Freedman.Diaconis", "Sqrt", "Sturges", "Rice", "Doane", and "Scott.Normal". (Default = "Sturges")

drop_fac

A numeric value specifying the factor by which to adjust the number of bins if the initial binning results in too many/few bins: the drop factor of Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.1, at least 0.3. The number of bins that bin_method gives a path is multiplied by drop_fac and the product is rounded up (see estBinSize()). (Default = 1).

verbose

Print detailed output in the console. (Default is TRUE)

bin_mem_col

A character string representing the name of the column in which cells per bin are stored. (Default is "scmp_bin_members").

bin_col

A character string representing the name of the column in which bin labels are stored. (Default is "scmp_bin").

bin_size_col

A character string representing the name of the column in which bin sizes per bin are stored. (Default is "scmp_bin_size").

bin_ptime_col

A character string representing the column name for binned Pseudotime values in 'Dense' data. (Default is "scmp_binned_pseudotime").

split_bins

If TRUE, divide the bins of a path that hold more cells than the mean plus the standard deviation of the bin sizes of the path (Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.2; see Details). (Default = FALSE).

prune_bins

If TRUE, remove the bins of a path that hold fewer cells than the mean minus the standard deviation of the bin sizes of the path (Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.2; see Details). (Default = FALSE).

assay_name

Name of the Assay in sparse data from which the counts are used. (Default = "counts").

drop_trails

If the paths have different lengths of the binned pseudotime, drop the bins from the path with more bins. (Default = FALSE).

aggregate

A character string specifying the method to aggregate counts within each cluster. Available options are 'mean' or 'sum'. (Default = "sum").

fill_gaps

If corresponding bin is missing for a time-point, pull the successive bins and fill the gaps.

additional_params

Pass additional parameters as a named list. See examples

Value

An object of class ScMaSigPro, with updated Dense slot.

Details

split_bins and prune_bins equalise the sizes of the bins of each path as Section 2.2 of Srivastava et al. (2024) describes: "scMaSigPro calculates the mean (\(\mu\)) and standard deviation (\(\sigma\)) of the sizes of all bins per path to establish maximum (\(\mu+\sigma\)) and minimum (\(\mu-\sigma\)) allowable bin sizes. Bins larger than the maximum size are divided, and those smaller than the minimum size can be optionally removed, ensuring uniform bin sizes. The process is repeated until all bins conform to the established size criteria." The mean and the standard deviation are those of the sizes of the bins that bin_method gives the path, empty bins included, and both limits are set once, before any bin is divided.

With split_bins = TRUE, a bin larger than the maximum is divided into the number of bins that bin_method and drop_fac give for its cells, rounded up, until no bin is larger; sc.squeeze() stops with an error when a division gives back bins it has already produced. A path with a single bin has no standard deviation and keeps its bin.

With prune_bins = TRUE, the bins smaller than the minimum are removed, after any division. When the standard deviation is larger than the mean, the minimum is negative and no bin is removed. The cells of a removed bin stay in the Sparse slot, but no bin of the Dense slot holds them.
